entities.name: Švitrigaila
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Švitrigaila (born unknown, died February 19, 1452) was a son of Algirdas, Grand Duke of Lithuania, and a prominent, albeit largely unsuccessful, contender for the Lithuanian throne during a turbulent period of dynastic and geopolitical realignments in Eastern Europe. His career, spanning several decades, was defined by persistent struggles against his cousins, particularly Vytautas the Great and later Sigismund Kęstutaitis, for control of the Grand Duchy and its orientation, oscillating between an independent, Eastern Orthodox-leaning Lithuania and one increasingly integrated with the Catholic Polish Crown. His brief tenure as Grand Duke from 1430 to 1432 marks a critical juncture in the Polish-Lithuanian union.

Following the death of his cousin Vytautas in 1430, Švitrigaila, supported by segments of the Ruthenian nobility and the Teutonic Knights, seized the title of Grand Duke. His reign was characterized by a staunch anti-Polish stance, seeking to dismantle the Union of Horodło (1413) and assert full Lithuanian sovereignty, even forging alliances with the Golden Horde and various Moldavian and Wallachian princes. This ambition directly clashed with the interests of Jogaila, King of Poland and Švitrigaila's own brother, who supported Sigismund Kęstutaitis. The ensuing civil war culminated in the decisive Battle of Pabaiskas on September 1, 1435, where Švitrigaila's forces, including a significant contingent of Teutonic Knights, suffered a crushing defeat at the hands of Sigismund's army.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Švitrigaila's persistent efforts to sever the Polish-Lithuanian union and his eventual defeat at Pabaiskas directly led to the consolidation of Jagiellonian power and a stronger union, shaping the future political landscape of Eastern Europe for centuries. His actions defined a critical period of internal struggle and external alignment for the Grand Duchy of Lithuania.
